newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar higher and rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar higher and rangebound.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were slightly higher in thin midday dealings with prices continuing to trade within recent ranges.
At 1130 EST, May was up 0.08 cent at 10.91 cents, having traded from 10.93 to 10.83 cents. The outer contracts were 0.08 to 0.05 higher.
Volume was estimated at 3,999 lots as of 1100 EST.
Floor sources said support from the trade at the open lifted prices and local and commission house buying followed to take May to its high.
Prices had eased sligthly and by midsession and were holding just under the day's highs.
Dealers said the market could maintain its dull tone until mid-April, when players begin rolling May positions into July and October, amid a dearth of news.
"There is no substitute for good offtake and we're just not getting that," a trader said.
Cyclone Justin, which has drenched some of the cotton crop in Queensland, Australia, was having no visible effect on the market.

The head of Mexico's main sugar workers' union said today that the 1996/97 harvest will produce a record 4.5 million tonnes. Mexican Sugar Chamber, the umbrella group for sugar mill owners, has put the crop at 4.365 million tonnes, down from the record 4.378 million tonnes produced last season.
Resistance in May remained at 11.05 cents and support at 10.68.
Open interest in most-active May fell 873 lots to 61,380 lots as of Friday's close.
